summary: Verified Bearer-token auth persistence fix end-to-end. Backend: 23/23 pytest tests pass — POST /api/auth/session schema (rejects invalid session_id with 400, missing body with 422), AuthResponse Pydantic model contains session_token field, GET /api/auth/me / GET /api/bookings / PATCH /api/bookings / GET /api/consultants / POST /api/auth/logout all honor Authorization: Bearer header, logout invalidates the session for subsequent calls. Frontend: homepage renders without JS errors, Sign In button visible while unauth, AuthModal exposes google-signin-btn and consultant-signin-btn. E2E simulation: seeded a consultant user+session in PostgreSQL, wrote the session_token into localStorage (panchtattwa_session_token), reloaded page → Sign In disappears, user name renders top-right, useAuth.checkAuth() calls /api/auth/me with Bearer header (200), bookings fetch returns 200. Confirms the localStorage-based token persistence works as designed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:285-293 still sets the httponly session cookie alongside returning session_token. With SameSite=None on a same-origin K8s ingress this is harmless but redundant; the cookie is effectively dead code now that the frontend relies on Bearer. Consider removing to reduce confusion, or keep but document the fallback.

useAuth.js: signOut() calls /api/auth/logout but only sends Bearer header — backend handles that path. Good. However if the Bearer call fails (network), token is still cleared locally — safer to swallow errors as done.
useAuth.js:73 stores session_token only when present in response; this is safe but silently no-ops if backend ever stops returning it — consider logging a warning to aid future debugging.

utils/auth.js authFetch always sets credentials: 'include' which is unnecessary for Bearer-token flow and may trigger preflight in some browsers. Could be omitted now that cookies are not the source of truth.

Backend get_current_user still prefers cookie over Bearer (line 183-187). For consistency with the new design, Bearer should arguably be primary or both checked equally — current order is fine but worth a comment.
ADMIN_EMAIL is still hardcoded to 'rahulsingh2k10@gmail.com' default ignoring backend/.env (carried forward from iteration 2).
